objectives: Explain the ways in which ownership of real estate is acquired.
Apply the pre-emption right of co-owners in a sale of a share.
Distinguish a building right, a right of use and a servitude, and say how each ends.
Explain acquisition by prescription and why it matters for the circumstantial verification.
Explain what the entry of a deed protects against, and the effect of a recorded claim.

cards.front: Name three ways to acquire ownership.
cards.back: Legal transaction, prescription, other ways in law such as inheritance (Art. 77 ЗС).
**10 years** of uninterrupted possession; **5 years** in good faith (Art. 79 ЗС).
Loss of possession for more than **six months** (Art. 81 ЗС).
Possession: control as **one's own**. Holding: control **not** as one's own, e.g. a tenant (Art. 68 ЗС).
They are **presumed equal** until the contrary is proven (Art. 30 ЗС).

cards.front: What must a co-owner present to the notary before selling a share to a third person?
cards.back: Written evidence of an **offer to the other co-owners on the same terms** and a written declaration that **no one accepted** (Art. 33 ЗС).

cards.front: Time limit for a co-owner's redemption claim?
Form of a voluntary partition of real estate?
cards.back: Written with **notarially certified signatures**; court permission if persons without capacity or absent persons take part (Art. 35 ЗС).

cards.front: Can common parts of a condominium be divided?
When does an unused building right lapse?
Material interest for a building right deed?
cards.back: **90%** of the market price of the land (Art. 96(2) ЗННД).

cards.front: Can the holder of a right of use sell it?
When does a right of use end?
cards.back: Death of the holder (unless shorter term), end of a legal entity, loss of the thing, **5 years** of non-use (Art. 59 ЗС).

cards.front: Form of a waiver of ownership of real estate?
cards.back: Written with **notarially certified signature**, and **entered** in the property register (Art. 100 ЗС).

cards.front: What is the effect of entering a deed first?
cards.back: An unentered act cannot be relied upon against a third person who acquired from the same owner earlier and **entered** first (Art. 113 ЗС).

quiz.question: A person has possessed a house in good faith on the basis of a defective deed for 6 years without interruption. What is the position?
options: The person can claim ownership by prescription, as 5 years are enough in good faith
The person needs 10 years in any case
Possession never gives ownership of real estate
quiz.explanation: 5 years in good faith, 10 years otherwise.

quiz.question: Three siblings own a house in shares 1/2, 1/4, 1/4. Nothing proves the shares. What does the law presume?
options: The shares stated by the oldest sibling
quiz.explanation: Shares are presumed equal until the contrary is proven.

quiz.question: A co-owner wants to sell her share to a stranger. What does the notary require?
options: Written evidence of an offer to the other co-owners on the same terms and her declaration that nobody accepted
The written consent of the other co-owners

quiz.question: A co-owner sold his share to a third person with a false declaration. Within what time can another co-owner sue to redeem it?
quiz.explanation: The redemption claim must be filed within two months of the sale.

quiz.question: A building right was granted in 2018. Construction never started. What is the position in 2026?
options: The right lapsed because it was not used for 5 years
It became ownership of the land
quiz.explanation: The right to build on somebody else's land lapses if not used for 5 years.

quiz.question: Parents donate their flat to their son and keep a life-long right of use. Who pays the property tax while the parents live there?
options: The parents as holders of the right of use
quiz.explanation: The holder of the right of use pays the costs of use, including taxes and fees.

quiz.question: May the holder of a right of use sell that right to a third person?
quiz.explanation: The holder of a right of use cannot transfer the right.

quiz.question: Which form does a voluntary partition of a plot between two co-owners need?
quiz.explanation: Art. 35 ЗС requires written form with notarially certified signatures.

quiz.question: An owner wants to waive ownership of a ruined barn. When is the waiver effective?
options: When made in writing with a notarially certified signature and entered in the property register
When the owner stops paying tax

quiz.question: A seller sold the same flat to A on Monday and to B on Tuesday. B's deed was entered first. Who is protected?
quiz.explanation: An unentered act cannot be relied upon against a third person who entered first.

quiz.question: A buyer of a car from a person who was not the owner acted in good faith. Did the buyer become the owner?
options: No, because the transfer of a car needs notarially certified signatures
Yes, good faith is always enough for movables
Yes, if the price was fair
quiz.explanation: Good-faith acquisition from a non-owner does not apply when the transfer needs a notarial deed or certified signatures.

quiz.question: What are the common parts of a condominium?
options: The land, the foundations, the roof, the stairs, the main installations and other parts for common use
quiz.explanation: Art. 38 ЗС lists the common parts; they cannot be divided.
